monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher HR — indicating a meaningful shift toward more demanding aerobic work. Efficiency and cadence have also improved, suggesting better neuromuscular coordination.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved from 13.42 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift among all metrics — reflecting better oxygen utilization at submaximal intensities.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s distance by 5.5 km and need only one more run to match last month’s session count. To maintain momentum, aim for 1–2 easy runs totaling ~8–10 km over the remaining 10 days.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.62 even as avg HR increased +4 bpm and avg pace improved — indicating improved cardiovascular economy, likely due to recent long runs (11.1 km on 6/7 and 6/16) and consistent Zone 3 work.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance with emerging Zone 4 stimulus
insights.body: Zone 3 time jumped from 19% (May) to 29% (June), while Zone 4 rose from 3% to 15% — a meaningful increase in threshold-level training that aligns with your faster paces (e.g., 3.0 km @ 6:32 min/km on 6/11, avg HR 144 bpm).

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff stabilizing
insights.body: Cadence increased +5 spm (146 → 151) while stride length remained stable (~69 cm across long runs) and vertical oscillation held steady at 7.7 cm — suggesting improved turnover without sacrificing flight time or form economy.

insights.title: Low-intensity recovery run underutilized
insights.body: Only 1 of 5 recent runs (6/19: 3.2 km @ 10:50 min/km, HR 112 bpm) was truly recovery-focused (Z1); Z1% dropped from 36% in May to 25% in June — increasing cumulative fatigue risk despite strong performance.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-min Zone 1 run (HR ≤125 bpm) within the next 3 days, keeping cadence ≥145 spm and vertical oscillation <7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: Z1 volume dropped 11 percentage points MoM and your most recent recovery run (6/19) showed elevated ground contact time (344 ms) — a sign of residual fatigue needing active recovery.

recommendations.action: Repeat a 3.0–3.5 km tempo segment at 6:30–6:40 min/km (target HR 142–146 bpm) during your next midweek run, using cadence ≥160 spm as a pacing cue
recommendations.reason: Your 6/11 run at 6:32 min/km (HR 144, cadence 162) produced 3.4 aerobic TE — the highest in your recent log — confirming this intensity is well-tolerated and productive.

recommendations.action: Add 3 × 30-sec strides post-run after your next easy session, focusing on landing under center of mass (stride length target: 68–70 cm) and vertical oscillation <7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time averaged 315 ms across long runs but spiked to 344 ms on your slowest run (6/19), suggesting neuromuscular fatigue — strides will reinforce efficient mechanics without adding load.

weekly_focus.description: Balance the gains from increased Zone 3/4 work with intentional low-HR recovery to consolidate adaptations and protect running economy.
